core_obligations: Choose a presentation of S and, for each localising element, write down the presentation of the localisation obtained by adjoining the inverting equation (proof lines 8354-8362).
Record that the resulting ideal is Koszul-regular because the localisation is a local complete intersection (proof lines 8362-8366).

For a prime containing the presentation ideal, choose a localising element not contained in it, pass to the extended ring and lift a basis of the conormal space to a sequence which by Nakayama generates the ideal after further localising (proof lines 8366-8375).

Compare dimensions to see the number of generators is the expected one, apply the independence-of-generators statement and then the truncation statement to conclude that the original presentation ideal is Koszul-regular locally, which is the assertion (proof lines 8375-8382).
proof_roadmap: Read off Koszul regularity there (proof lines 8362-8366).
Lift a conormal basis and generate the ideal by Nakayama (proof lines 8366-8375).
Use independence of generators and truncation to conclude (proof lines 8375-8383).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that being a local complete intersection for a ring map can be checked after localising at finitely many elements generating the unit ideal, and the proof is a 30-line computation with presentations. Starting from a presentation of the target it writes down a presentation of each localisation by adding the equation inverting one of the localising elements, records that the resulting ideal is Koszul-regular, and then for a chosen prime lifts a basis of the conormal space to a sequence which by Nakayama generates the ideal after localising; comparing dimensions shows the number of generators is the expected one, the independence-of-generators statement converts a generating Koszul-regular sequence into the specific lifted one, and the truncation statement of the same section descends the Koszul-regularity back to the original ring. Three named statements of the chapter are used at precisely identified steps.
